title: Post-interview reflection: LLM Runtime candidate — Julie Kim
body:
Quick context and purpose:
This is my personal, somewhat messy post-loop note after the interview loop with the candidate (took place 2025-11-03). Intended as a scratchpad for Samir/Lena and for my own memory before we consolidate a formal scorecard. Not polished — internal thoughts, questions I still have, and a raw recommendation.

TL;DR recommendation:
- Lean hire (strong engineer, good infra instincts). Recommend follow-up on system design edgecases and a short homework (latency/cost tradeoff writeup). Possible hire at senior+ level if homework looks good.

High-level impressions (first pass):
- Presentation: calm, structured, answers in clear steps. Used whiteboard effectively for the KV cache flow explanation.
- Breadth: good across systems and ML infra; familiarity with GPU memory optimization, sharding, and quantization tradeoffs at a practical level.
- Depth: strong on run loop concerns (KV cache eviction, batching heuristics), weaker on low-level kernel optimization specifics (couldn't name a few kernel-level ops we asked about).
- Product sense: solid. Asked clarifying questions about SLAs, graceful degradation, and how client-side fallbacks should be surfaced to product.

Notes from each interview segment:
1) Systems design (Samir) — ~50m
- Asked candidate to design an inference runtime component that supports multi-tenant KV caching and prefetching. Candidate sketched: per-tenant cache namespaces, LRU with pinning for high-priority keys, proactive prefetch based on request templates.
- Good: explicitly called out cold-start penalty, and suggested a fast path for short-seq requests that bypasses KV merge.
- Missed: didn't quantify eviction impact on tail latency (no examples of how they'd measure/experiment). Also didn't mention how to coordinate cache invalidation across replicas under autoscaling.
- Follow-up question: how would you test the effectiveness of proactive prefetch? Candidate suggested synthetic traffic and real traffic shadowing but didn't propose specific metrics (I would expect hit-rate delta + downstream latency P95).

2) Serving runtime internals (Lena) — ~45m
- Topics: batching strategies, continuous batching vs fixed-window, memory pinning, quantization fallback.
- Strong points: explained continuous batching heuristics well, suggested adaptive thresholds based on observed sequence length distribution, and described KV cache persistence to local NVMe for quick warm-up.
- Weaker points: when asked about mixed-precision numeric issues (FP16->int8), the candidate spoke high-level tradeoffs but could not cite concrete mitigations for degenerate cases (per-token hallucination regressions after aggressive quantization).
- Technical curiosity: candidate brought up an idea about leveraging model-aware batching (grouping by context template similarity) — interesting and could be low-effort win.

3) ML/Model ops familiarity (me, Julie) — ~30m
- Covered model versioning, rollout policies, semantic compatibility between model variants. Candidate demonstrated knowledge of canarying and shadow traffic but less experience with evaluation suites (prompt-based regressions).
- Noted: limited hands-on with SLO-linked quality monitoring. Has seen tooling but hasn't owned it.

4) Behavioral / culture fit (~20m)
- Communication: clear, asks for examples, ties technical choices to product impact.
- Collaboration: described previous cross-team project where they worked with Platform + Product to throttle requests during holiday peaks; this aligned with our needs.
- Red flags: minimal. Candidate prefers small, focused teams — might not want large org responsibilities.

Rough scorecard (my private quick scores 1-5):
- System design: 4/5 (good structure, missing quantification)
- Runtime internals: 4/5 (practical, good heuristics)
- ML ops / evaluations: 3/5 (needs ramp on eval tooling)
- Communication / collaboration: 5/5
- Overall fit for Senior+ role: 4/5

Hard/soft tradeoffs observed:
- Strength in pragmatic infra — likely to move quickly on performance/latency projects and shipping operational improvements.
- Needs mentoring on setting up eval/quality pipelines tied to rollouts (we have senior members who could pair on that).
- Might be more excited by low-latency, high-throughput components than managing cross-org product programs.

Unresolved questions / homework I want to send before making final rec:
1) Short written exercise (1-2 pages): pick one of these and write 3–4 concrete experiments you would run to evaluate impact on P95 latency and per-token cost for a new batching strategy. Include instrumentation metrics and expected risk.
2) Small systems question: how would you handle cache invalidation when replicas scale down quickly? Ask for sequence diagram and metric triggers.
3) Ask for concrete example of a time they diagnosed a regression caused by quantization or precision change (what was the root cause, how discovered, what mitigations).

Operational notes (logistics):
- Compensation expectations: mentioned target band slightly above our posted for senior, said flexible for right role. Will need to clarify.
- Availability: 4 weeks notice.
- Citizenship / remote: based in PNW, ok with hybrid.

Possible hiring outcomes to propose to committee:
- Option A (strong): Extend offer at Senior+ with pairing/training on eval tooling; brief homework required.
- Option B (conservative): Another loop focused on low-level kernel/QAT and quantization regression debugging.
- Option C (pass): If homework shows weak experiment design or lack of root-cause examples.

My next steps (Julie):
- Draft a concise scorecard (formal) and share with Samir and Lena by 2025-11-07.
- Send the two homework prompts if team agrees.
- Confirm compensation band with People Ops before final rec.

Notes-to-self (rambling):
- Candidate's model-aware batching idea felt like something we can prototype quickly; assign to infra intern? Good quick win.
- Remember to ask PeopleOps whether 4-week notice plus start-of-Q1 relocation comp adjustments are a blocker for urgent hires.

End of scratchpad.
